judgments.reasoning_cat1: The same-day/next-day split is clear in structure but hinges entirely on 'Margin Notice Deadline' and 'close of business in the relevant market', both undefined in operation. That is a nameable vagueness.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short attribution rule requiring agreement; simple though it provides no default if the parties do not agree. Small gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A permissive threshold provision expressly requiring prior agreement on the amount or percentage. Definite.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permissive election to margin transaction-by-transaction rather than on the aggregate; drafting is explicit about the calculation basis. Little to construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'as Buyer shall reasonably determine in its discretion' pairs a reasonableness standard with discretion, and the conditions (A) and (B) suspending payment are broadly worded. Moderate intrinsic softness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex I ¶4 (c071) renumbers this sentence as 5(a) and bolts on tax gross-up provisions with their own income-payment concept, and Paragraph 8 preserves Buyer's Income obligations; harmonising the original and amended Paragraph 5 takes work. Real but manageable strain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sale-versus-loan hedge ('Although the parties intend ... in the event any such Transactions are deemed to be loans') is a deliberately conditional characterisation that courts routinely have to construe. The deeming language is nonetheless standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex I ¶2 (c069) restates the sale intent, Paragraph 8 passes all of Seller's interest to Buyer, and Annex I ¶8's replacement Paragraph 12 (c085) grants a separate mutual security interest — overlapping grants that must be reconciled. judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clauses (i), (ii) and (iii) are joined disjunctively so it is unclear whether the documentation requirement in (i) applies to book-entry or other transfers; 'any other method mutually acceptable' is an open catch-all. A modest general-versus-specific point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere prescribes a transfer mechanic that contradicts this, and Annex I is silent on settlement mechanics. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To the extent required by applicable law' makes the segregation duty conditional on an unspecified body of law, and the rehypothecation permission is broad. Contestable but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says all of Seller's interest passes to Buyer, which sits against the deemed pledge in Paragraph 6 (c032) and against the Required Disclosure (c035) contemplating Seller-held securities and clearing liens. Those need harmonising.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision is reproduced with its alternatives unresolved — '[will]* [may]**', '[its clearing bank] [third parties]**', '[the clearing]* [any]**' — so the operative words were never selected, a mechanical defect that changes meaning. judgments.reasoning_cat2: It states Seller may not substitute unless Buyer grants the right, while Paragraph 9(b) (c037) deems Buyer to have granted exactly that in custody transactions and Annex I ¶11(c) (c088) adds a further substitution right. judgments.reasoning_cat1: Substitution requires Buyer's agreement and acceptance, stated plainly with a deeming rule for the substituted securities. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 9(b) (c037) deems that agreement given in custody transactions and Annex I ¶11(c) (c088) creates a notice-based right subject to Buyer's veto, so three different substitution regimes coexist. That layering invites argument about which controls.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deemed advance consent qualified by a Market Value equivalence proviso; the proviso inherits the Market Value vagueness but the rule itself is clear. Moderate-low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It effectively cancels the agreement requirement in 9(a) (c036) for custody transactions and cuts against the Required Disclosure (c035) premise that Seller cannot substitute. Also overlaps Annex I ¶11(c)'s new consent mechanism.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional five-part representation with an agency carve-out; each limb is definite. Nothing ambiguous to name.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex I ¶6 has CSFB Corporation act as Agent for both parties, which must be squared with the 'as principal' representation in (ii), though the carve-out for disclosed principals largely handles it. Modest tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed enumerated list of seven Events of Default with 'material respect' as the only soft term; expressio unius arguments about what is not listed are available. Moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex I ¶8's replacement Paragraph 12 (c085) declares that a default under any other agreement 'whatsoever' is an Event of Default hereunder, adding to what this paragraph presents as exhaustive. That is a real cross-provision strain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The automatic deemed exercise on an Act of Insolvency, coupled with an obligation to give notice 'as promptly as practicable' except in that case, is clear if unusual. Low intrinsic ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates with the Repurchase Date definition (c018) and Paragraph 19 safe-harbour intent (c060, c061); the Annex adds no competing acceleration except the Tax Event mechanism. Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three specified consequences, each mechanical; 'any other amounts owing hereunder' is a mild catch-all. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 11(a), 11(d)(i) and the Income provisions in Paragraph 5, and with the replacement Paragraph 12's setoff. Nothing contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Transfer of title on tender of the aggregate Repurchase Prices; clear conditional structure. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Works with 11(d)(ii), 11(f) and the 11(g) cap; no competing provision on defaulting-Buyer remedies. Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: It relies on a 'generally recognized source', which Paragraph 11(e) (c044) and Annex I ¶7 (c084) address differently, and the replacement Paragraph 12 (c085) extends 11(d)(i) to non-Agreement obligations. Those interactions add real strain.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: It opens 'Unless otherwise provided in Annex I', and Annex I ¶7 (c084) does provide a pricing source for Market Value, so whether that displaces this discretion is genuinely open; the Market Value definition (c011) requires an agreed source instead. A real internal pull.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific damages measure for the defaulting-Buyer case, defined by reference to fixed quantities. Definite.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-directional cap stated with a precise measuring date. Clear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short preservation-of-rights sentence in standard form. Nothing to construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional obligation that CSFB Corporation confirm each Transaction on the Purchase Date; the condition and duty are stated plainly. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expands on ¶6.a (c081) and is limited by ¶6.b(ii)'s liability disclaimer (c083); nothing in the body contradicts it beyond the confirmation-delivery point in 3(b). Modest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The disclaimer is broad but carves out gross negligence, wilful misconduct and securities-law non-compliance, and 'no responsibility or personal liability' is clear enough. Moderate-low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It confers rights and burdens on CSFB Corporation, a signatory only 'solely in its capacity as agent' and not a Buyer or Seller, which must be squared with the two-party structure and Paragraph 10's 'as principal' representation (c038). A real but secondary tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It names three screen sources and then, where no price is available, makes CSFB (Hong Kong) or 'one of its affiliates' the pricing source — a one-sided valuation power with no standard of reasonableness attached. 'If a price is not available' is itself an elastic trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts across the Market Value definition (c011), which requires a 'generally recognized source agreed to by the parties', and against Paragraph 11(e) (c044), which gives the nondefaulting party (which may be Seller) the sole discretion to establish the source. Those three cannot be harmonised without choosing a winner.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any other agreement or transaction whatsoever' and 'all transactions and agreements between them' are unbounded catch-alls that convert any outside default into an Event of Default, and the security interest reaches all property 'transferred ... pursuant to this Agreement or otherwise'. The breadth is nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces Paragraph 12 (c050), adds Events of Default beyond the closed list in Paragraph 11 (c039), and reaches outside agreements despite the supersession language in Paragraph 14 (c052). Several relationships require construction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional FIRREA record-keeping representation, with specific and verifiable content. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It adds to the Paragraph 10 representations (c038) expressly and matches Paragraph 19(c) and Annex I ¶10. Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Statutory characterisation language mirroring Paragraph 19(a), with the same self-limiting carve-out. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplements Paragraph 19 (c060) consistently rather than displacing it. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'substantially the same Securities' is undefined and elastic, and the notice timing ('at or prior to 10:00 am ... on such business day') has no clear antecedent for which business day is meant; the closing duty that Buyer 'shall offer Seller the right to terminate' is also unspecified as to terms. Several nameable soft points.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It layers a third substitution regime on Paragraph 9(a)'s consent requirement (c036) and 9(b)'s deemed consent (c037), and its opening condition ('does not have any existing right to substitute') may be defeated by 9(b) itself. That circularity is a genuine incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the loss incurred by Buyer directly arising or resulting from' a substitution, 'solely determined and calculated by Buyer in good faith', puts an open-ended measure in one party's hands. The good-faith qualifier is the only check.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It charges Seller with hedge and replacement-transaction costs on a substitution or termination, which sits against Annex I ¶13's bar on indirect and consequential loss (c091) and duplicates the Paragraph 11(h) damages measure (c047) outside default. Reconcilable only with effort.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short non-reliance representation with 'as it deems necessary' as the only soft phrase. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits Paragraph 10's representations and the disclosures in Paragraph 20 without contradiction. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL LOSS OR DAMAGES' is the classic contested boundary, especially against hedge-unwind and replacement costs. The categories are named but their edges are notoriously disputed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 11(h)(ii)-(iii) (c047) expressly awards hedge-termination and replacement-transaction damages and 'any other loss ... directly arising', and Annex I ¶11(d) (c089) does the same on substitution, yet this clause says 'UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCES'. That is a direct clash a court would have to resolve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It submits to 'EXCLUSIVE JURISDICTION' but 'SOLELY FOR THE PURPOSE OF ANY SUIT ... BROUGHT TO ENFORCE ITS OBLIGATIONS HEREUNDER OR RELATING IN ANY WAY TO THIS AGREEMENT' — whether the exclusivity is a limit on the parties or only on the submission is arguable. That tension is nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the New York governing law clause (c055); Paragraph 11(i)'s preservation of other rights (c049) does not displace it. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard, unqualified jury waiver. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the forum clause immediately preceding it; nothing elsewhere contemplates jury trial. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence with no defined temporal or substantive limits: 'covers all Transactions in effect as of the date hereof' does not say on what terms pre-existing Transactions are converted. Its brevity leaves the retroactive effect open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with Paragraph 14 (c052), which supersedes prior general terms and conditions, and with the misdated Annex preamble (c067) fixing 'the date hereof'; whether pre-existing Confirmations survive on their original terms is genuinely open. A real cross-provision question.
